items.title: Movement restricted under Section 144 in some areas of South Waziristan, Tank on Monday
items.description: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: The administrations of Lower South Waziristan, Upper South Waziristan and Tank have imposed Section 144 in several areas of the three districts for August 10 (Monday), citing security concerns and directing residents to avoid unnecessary movement during the specified hours. Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) is a legal provision that empowers district administrations to prohibit an assembly of four or more people in an area for a limited period. The deputy commissioners (DCs) of the three districts issued separate notifications on Sunday evening, imposing restrictions on movement between 6am and 7pm, as well as ordering the closure of markets and business centres in the specified areas. According to the notification issued by the Lower South Waziristan administration, a curfew will remain in force in Wana tehsil from 6am to 7pm on Monday. During the curfew, all kinds of movement will remain prohibited, and markets and business centres in certain areas will remain closed. DC Musarrat Zaman said several important roads and connecting routes in and around Wana would also remain closed to general traffic during the restrictions. The affected routes include the road from Wana through Tiarza Gate, Karb Kot, Tanai and Azizabad Chowk up to Dargai Bridge. The route from Gul Kuch through Toi Khullah to Tanai has also been included in the restricted areas. The administration said movement on the affected routes would only be allowed in an emergency and with prior permission from the police or security forces. People travelling for an emergency would be required to produce their national identity cards and other relevant documents to security personnel. Residents have also been directed to follow the instructions of security personnel during the curfew. According to the notification, vehicles approaching security forces must be stopped around 50 metres before the personnel, and all occupants must get out of the vehicle. The administration warned that any violation of the restrictions would be the responsibility of the individual concerned and could lead to legal action. Meanwhile, Upper South Waziristan DC Irfan Ali said Section 144 would remain in force in the Sarwekai and Ladha tehsils of Upper South Waziristan from 6am to 7pm on Monday. All kinds of movement would remain restricted in the notified areas, while markets and business centres would remain closed during the period. Several major routes in Upper South Waziristan have also been declared out of bounds. These include the route from Ladha through Makeen, Tabai Sar, Bibi Raghzai, Kotkai and Spinkai Raghzai to Nazar Khel. The route from Dargai Bridge through Medi Jan, Sheen Warsak, Mola Khan Sarai and Chagmalai to Jandola has also been included in the restrictions. Similarly, the route from Sarwekai through Mola Khan Sarai to Barwand will remain closed to general traffic during the notified period. The Upper South Waziristan administration said only emergency movement would be permitted on the affected roads and that travellers would have to obtain permission from the police or security forces. The administration has also directed motorists to stop their vehicles at least 50 metres before reaching security personnel and for all passengers to get out of the vehicles. It warned that unauthorised movement or violation of the restrictions would invite action under the law. In Tank district, DC Jamshed Khan said Section 144 would be enforced in Jandola subdivision from 6am to 7pm on Monday. The restrictions would cover Jandola bazaar and other notified areas, where all business centres would remain closed and general movement would be prohibited during the specified hours. According to the notification issued by the Tank administration, the route from Kour fort through Khargai to Jandola and up to the boundary between Tank district and Upper South Waziristan would remain closed. Jandola bazaar has also been included in the restricted area. Another affected route runs from Dabra through Kour fort, Gardavi, Gomal Zam Dam and Gulgi Kot to Dabra and up to the boundary between Tank district and Lower South Waziristan. Kor bazaar has also been included in the restrictions. The three district administrations have appealed to residents, traders, transporters and travellers to avoid unnecessary movement during the specified hours and remain at home unless there is an unavoidable emergency. The restrictions are expected to affect movement between the three districts, which are geographically connected through several major roads and link routes. The authorities have therefore included some inter-district routes in the notifications to regulate movement during the specified period. Residents have been urged to plan their travel accordingly and avoid the affected routes on August 10 to prevent inconvenience. The district administrations of Upper South Waziristan and Lower South Waziristan had also imposed Section 144 in several areas in June due to security concerns and the movement of security forces. South Waziristan, as well as the rest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, has been facing terrorism for a long time. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July , making it the deadliest month of 2026.

items.title: NAF air strikes kill nine ISWAP fighters, commander in Borno
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigerian Air Force, NAF, has reported the killing of nine Islamic State West Africa Province, ISWAP, fighters, including a senior commander, in an air strike in Borno State. The operation was conducted on Saturday, August 8, 2026, following intelligence on the activities and movement of suspected terrorists within the Sambisa Forest area. Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday. Ejodame said the operation followed the deployment of a Remotely Piloted Aircraft, RPA, for persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance, ISR, which enabled the military to track a group of terrorists moving towards a suspected hideout. He said the aircraft conducted a precision strike after the target was positively identified and confirmed. “Subsequent battle damage assessment indicated significant effects on the targeted compound, with several terrorists neutralised,” he said. According to him, further intelligence received after the operation confirmed that nine ISWAP fighters were killed, while several others were wounded. Among those reportedly killed was Abu Khalid Al Muhajir, described by the NAF as an ISWAP commander responsible for providing security escorts for the movement of senior members of the group. The NAF said his death was expected to affect the group’s movement and protection arrangements, particularly because of his reported knowledge of routes and terrain connecting terrorist enclaves within the Sambisa Forest and surrounding areas. Ejodame said intelligence also indicated that some of the terrorists affected by the strike were linked to elements suspected of involvement in the recent ambush of Nigerian troops along the Bita-Yamtage axis in Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State. He said the operation demonstrated the growing effectiveness of intelligence-led air operations, particularly the use of persistent surveillance and precision strikes to locate and engage terrorist elements. The NAF said the operation was also expected to disrupt the movement of senior ISWAP members and coordination of activities across the group’s enclaves. Ejodame assured that the Nigerian Air Force would continue to conduct intelligence-led air operations in coordination with ground forces to degrade terrorist capabilities, restrict their freedom of movement and improve security for communities affected by insurgency in the North-East. items.title: INEC extends deadline for submission of nominations for state elections to August 11
items.description: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has extended the deadline for the submission of the list of candidates for the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections for the 2027 general elections to Aug. 11. Mr Mohammed Haruna, INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information Voter Education Committee, announced the extension in a statement in Abuja. Haruna noted that the extension of the deadline for the upload of nominations onto the commission’s dedicated portal followed appeals by political parties. “The submission window, which, according to the revised timetable and schedule of activities for the general elections, was originally scheduled to close on Saturday, Aug. 8, has been extended to Tuesday, Aug. 11. “The extension follows growing appeals by political parties for additional time to complete the process,” he said. Haruna also notified voters who applied for replacement of lost, damaged or defaced permanent voter cards (PVCs) that the window to print downloadable copies of their cards would expire by midnight of Aug. 9. This, according to him, is to allow the commission to compile the data of downloaded PVCs for final statistics of the total PVCs collected ahead of the Aug. 15 Osun governorship election. He recalled that PVC collection in Osun was held at the registration area (RA) level from July 22 to July 28. “Owing to complaints of large crowds and difficulties encountered by voters at collection centres, the commission approved an extension of RA-level collection to July 31, before collection moved to LGA level, running from Aug. 1 to Aug. 7. “The commission also wishes to state that replacement of downloadable PVCs has been made available to voters in Odo-Otin and Ife Central local government areas whose cards were carted away by hoodlums who invaded the two centres. “The commission reiterates that the stolen cards cannot be used to vote,” he said. Haruna reassured the people of Osun of INEC’s readiness to conduct a free, fair, credible and inclusive governorship election on Aug. 15. The post INEC extends deadline for submission of nominations for state elections to August 11 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kiiraay : les structures de base au cœur de la stratégie d’implantation
items.description: Le parti Kiiraay – Les Patriotes Républicains veut désormais passer à une nouvelle étape de son développement avec la mise en place progressive de ses structures de base. Dans un message aux militants, le président du parti, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, a appelé à faire de l’implantation territoriale et de la mobilisation militante les principales priorités de la formation politique. Après l’engouement suscité par la création du parti, le président de Kiiraay préconise d’abord l’installation de cellules dans les quartiers et les villages. Cette phase devra également permettre la massification, l’organisation de la base et la mise en place de comités d’initiative chargés de préparer les différents mouvements prévus par les statuts. Ces mouvements concerneront notamment les jeunes, les femmes, les cadres, les sages, les personnes handicapées, les enseignants, les doomu daara, les artisans et les transporteurs. Le processus se poursuivra avec le placement des cartes de membres, avant l’installation officielle des sections, coordinations et mouvements statutaires. L’objectif affiché est de renforcer la présence de Kiiraay dans l’ensemble des territoires, mais également au sein de la diaspora. Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye souligne que les structures de proximité doivent constituer « le fondement » de l’organisation du parti. Elles devront, selon lui, favoriser le rassemblement autour du projet politique, recueillir les préoccupations des populations et contribuer à la promotion d’initiatives de développement local. Le président de Kiiraay met, par ailleurs, l’accent sur la nécessité d’une implantation ouverte et inclusive. Il demande que les différentes structures reflètent « la diversité des forces vives » des localités concernées. Pour encadrer ce processus, le parti prévoit un mécanisme de validation. Les cellules, sections communales, coordinations et mouvements devront ainsi être approuvés par des commissaires politiques désignés selon des règles qui seront précisées dans une prochaine circulaire.

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Las comunidades religiosas de Ceuta se concentran para reclamar una respuesta inmediata a la crisis migratoria
items.description: Cientos de personas se han congregado en la tarde de este domingo en la plaza de la Constitución de Ceuta en una protesta convocada por las comunidades religiosas de la ciudad autónoma para reclamar una respuesta “inmediata, decidida y proporcionada” de las autoridades a la crisis migratoria generada por la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en la ciudad autónoma el 30 de julio. Entre los manifestantes se repiten las críticas al Gobierno, al que se culpa de inacción y de “abandono”, y la reivindicación de que “Ceuta es España”. “Pedro Sánchez, dimisión”, han coreado al inicio de la concentración. En el otro extremo, ha recibido un apoyo masivo el presidente ceutí, Juan Jesús Vivas (PP), quien ha mostrado su apoyo a la iniciativa y ha insistido en desvincularla de “cualquier partido”. Por otro lado, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Italia, Antonio Tajani, ha tachado de “desproporcionada” la decisión del presidente del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, de restablecer controles fronterizos a viajeros procedentes de Italia, en lo que describió como una “represalia” a la suspensión italiana del acuerdo Schengen con España; circunstancia que, ha apuntado Tajani, espera revertir cuando termine “el peligro” de una supuesta segunda incursión masiva en Ceuta desde Marruecos. items.title: Gumi urges Islamic scholars to join politics, seek elective offices
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — Kaduna-based Islamic scholar, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has urged Islamic scholars across the country to participate actively in politics and seek elective and appointive positions. Gumi made the call in an interview with the BBC Hausa Service monitored by our correspondent, arguing that Islam does not prohibit Islamic scholars, or Ulama, from participating in politics or governance. He said the involvement of Islamic scholars in politics could contribute to greater emphasis on morality, accountability and responsible leadership. According to him, “there is nothing in Islam that prevents an Islamic scholar from participating in politics or occupying a political office.” The cleric said Ulama had responsibilities that extended beyond their traditional religious roles, including contributing to the development and leadership of society. Gumi argued that Islamic scholars could provide effective leadership because of their religious training, knowledge of Islamic principles and emphasis on accountability before God. He said leaders guided by faith and moral values would be more conscious of their responsibilities to the people. The cleric therefore encouraged Islamic scholars to consider participating in politics and contesting elective positions instead of leaving the political space exclusively to professional politicians. He maintained that political leadership should not be regarded as the exclusive preserve of professional politicians, stressing that Islamic scholars, like other citizens, had a role to play in shaping society and providing leadership when given the opportunity. The post Gumi urges Islamic scholars to join politics, seek elective offices appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Alassane Diatta, milieu de Villarreal : le pari d’un futur patron de l’entrejeu des Lions
items.description: À 21 ans, Alassane Diatta poursuit une progression régulière qui attire déjà l’attention des observateurs du football sénégalais. Formé au pays avant de rejoindre Villarreal, le jeune milieu de terrain construit son avenir dans l’un des clubs espagnols les plus réputés pour le développement des talents. Son parcours patient et ambitieux nourrit l’espoir d’un futur renfort pour l’entrejeu de l’équipe nationale du Sénégal. Dans le football moderne, les trajectoires les plus solides ne sont pas toujours les plus bruyantes. Celle d’Alassane Diatta s’écrit loin des projecteurs, mais avec une constance qui force le respect. Né le 14 mai 2005 en Casamance, le jeune milieu sénégalais a franchi les étapes une à une avant de rejoindre Villarreal, club reconnu pour son travail de formation et de valorisation des jeunes joueurs. Avant l’Espagne, Diatta a été formé au Sénégal, notamment à Mbour Petite-Côte puis à Keur Madior FC. C’est dans ces structures qu’il développe les qualités qui caractérisent aujourd’hui son jeu : un grand volume de course, une présence physique importante, une bonne lecture du jeu et une capacité à participer aussi bien à la récupération qu’à la construction. En novembre 2023, Villarreal décide de miser sur lui et lui fait signer un premier contrat de quatre ans. Le choix du club espagnol n’est pas anodin. Le « Sous-marin jaune » s’est forgé une réputation de tremplin pour de nombreux jeunes talents, avec une transition progressive entre les équipes de formation, la réserve et l’équipe première. À Villarreal, Alassane Diatta aura également l’occasion d’évoluer aux côtés d’un autre Sénégalais, le milieu international Pape Alassane Gueye, une proximité qui pourrait faciliter son intégration et enrichir son apprentissage au plus haut niveau. L’apprentissage du football espagnol constitue souvent un test décisif pour les jeunes joueurs africains. Alassane Diatta l’a abordé avec patience. Après une première phase d’adaptation dans les catégories de jeunes, il rejoint Villarreal B en Primera Federación, le troisième niveau espagnol, où il accumule les minutes et gagne en maturité tactique. Au fil des mois, le Sénégalais s’impose comme un élément de plus en plus important de l’entrejeu de la réserve. Sa capacité à couvrir les espaces, à gagner des duels et à relancer proprement attire l’attention du staff professionnel. Une étape symbolique est franchie en décembre 2024 lorsqu’il effectue ses débuts avec l’équipe première de Villarreal en Coupe du Roi. La confiance du club se confirme un an plus tard. En décembre 2025, Villarreal prolonge son contrat jusqu’en juin 2030. Une décision qui traduit la volonté de sécuriser un joueur considéré comme un investissement d’avenir. Ce qui rend le profil d’Alassane Diatta particulièrement intéressant pour le Sénégal, c’est sa complémentarité potentielle avec les milieux déjà installés chez les Lions. Le Sénégal dispose de joueurs d’expérience comme Idrissa Gana Gueye et de jeunes talents comme Lamine Camara, Pape Matar Sarr ou Pape Gueye. Diatta apporte un registre différent : celui d’un milieu puissant, capable de récupérer, de se projeter et de casser les lignes par la passe. Avec son gabarit imposant et son activité constante, il correspond au prototype du milieu « box-to-box » recherché dans le football actuel. Son impact dans les duels aériens et sa capacité à répéter les efforts peuvent devenir des atouts précieux dans les compétitions internationales. À court terme, une convocation en équipe A semble encore prématurée. Le joueur doit d’abord s’installer durablement dans le football professionnel espagnol et gagner davantage de temps de jeu avec l’équipe première de Villarreal. Mais son nom figure déjà parmi les jeunes milieux sénégalais les plus suivis par les recruteurs et les observateurs. L’histoire récente du football sénégalais montre que les passages par Villarreal peuvent servir de véritable accélérateur de carrière. Le club espagnol a déjà accompagné l’éclosion de joueurs sénégalais avant leur explosion au plus haut niveau européen. Alassane Diatta espère désormais suivre cette voie, avec son propre style et sa propre histoire. Parti des terrains de Casamance pour atteindre les portes de la Liga, le jeune milieu incarne une génération qui avance sans brûler les étapes. Et si sa progression se poursuit au même rythme, le Sénégal pourrait tenir, dans les prochaines années, bien plus qu’une promesse : un véritable candidat à la relève au cœur du milieu de terrain des Lions. C.T.N.

items.title: Sindh govt decides judicial commission to probe Mir Raza Ali murder case
items.description: KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to seek a judicial commission to probe the killing of 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali, Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Sunday. Ali’s body was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide. However, after injury details from a second postmortem ruled out the possibility of suicide, a murder charge was added to the case on Sunday. “A decision has been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry into the murder case of Mir Raza Ali Khan,” the Sindh home minister said in a statement issued by his office. According to the statement, Lanjar, along with Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, visited Ali’s residence to meet his parents. They assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Lanjar said the judicial commission would be constituted under the leadership of a Sindh High Court judge on the recommendation of the Sindh chief minister. During the meeting, Lanjar briefed Ali’s parents in detail about the progress of the case and the investigation, the statement said. “The investigation team will maintain full contact and cooperation with the deceased’s parents,” the minister was quoted as saying. “A transparent and impartial investigation into the case will be ensured.” He affirmed that all requirements of justice would be fulfilled and no leniency would be shown to anyone responsible. Meanwhile, the Karachi mayor noted that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah chaired a four-hour-long meeting during which “all aspects of the incident and the investigation were reviewed in detail”. The decision of a judicial inquiry comes after Faryal Talpur, the chairperson of Sindh Assembly’s Standing Committee on Home, recommended that CM Murad constitute a judicial commission for a “transparent, impartial and comprehensive investigation” into the case. Taking notice of Ali’s murder, she said the proposed commission should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light. “Legal and disciplinary action should be taken without discrimination against those found responsible in light of the commission’s findings,” Talpur added. She further stressed that justice for the victim’s family must be ensured at all costs and that the public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case. “No negligence or bias will be tolerated in meeting the requirements of justice,” she said, adding that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system were fundamental responsibilities of the government and relevant institutions. 2 officers suspended Separately, Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan ordered the immediate suspension of Sharea Faisal sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi. They were suspended over “failure to preserve the crime scene and carry out proper crime scene investigation”, AIG Khan told Dawn . According to a statement released by his office, the additional IG also ordered SHO Qureshi’s reversion to a lower rank. “The full implementation of rules, regulations and accountability principles in departmental affairs would be ensured,” the statement said. “Action will be taken in accordance with the law and rules in case of any violation of discipline by an officer.” New police team for probe Earlier on Sunday, an order released by the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death. It also showed that the murder charge had been added to the first information report (FIR) on his father’s complaint. The order, seen by Dawn , said the new investigating team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem, to “supervise the investigation of FIR no. 795/2026 u/s 365/ 302/ 201 of the PPC”. Initially, the FIR was registered only under Section 365 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), which pertains to kidnapping. Of the newly added provisions, Section 302 pertains to murder and Section 201 to hiding the evidence of an offence or giving false information to screen the offender. The case would now be probed by a five-member team led by Sindh Deputy IG (Crime and Investigation) Amir Farooqui and comprising Rapid Response Force Al-Falah SSP Syed Muhammad Ali Raza, Korangi SP (Investigation) Qais Khan, Central SP (Investigation) Anam Tajjamul and Zaman Town SIO Ch. Ghazanfar, the police order said. It added: “The team shall undertake a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the case from all relevant angles. The team shall identify, collect, preserve and examine any new or additional evidence and shall thoroughly examine and analyse all physical, technical, circumstantial and forensic evidence collected during the investigation. “The team shall make all out efforts to work out the case and submit a report to the court concerned within the stipulated period. The team may co-opt any officer to assist in the investigation. Progress shall be reported on a day-to-day basis.” On Saturday, the lawyer for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, had demanded that the first investigation probing the case be replaced, after a fresh post-mortem examination conducted following the exhumation of Ali’s body found that he had been shot in the back — evidence that ruled out the possibility of suicide. Speaking to the media, he reiterated the allegation that Ali had been tortured before being murdered. “This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged. The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”. Advocate Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed. Controversy over autopsy Ali, an Institute of Business Administration graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The latest developments in his case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination. Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission. On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board. However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan. On Friday morning, Ali’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was deferred after they objected ti the new board. Standing alongside Ali’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board on Friday, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday. After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn, “We have collected samples for identification, chemical analysis and gunshot residue. The cause of death is reserved for laboratory reports.” Regarding the autopsy, she said that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said. She said the body bore “injuries in right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in mouth and throat”.

items.title: SERAP trains Benue communities on security tracking, accountability
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi MAKURDI — The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project, SERAP, has urged residents of Benue State to become more proactive in accessing justice, monitoring government activities and demanding accountability when public spending does not translate into improved safety and wellbeing. The call was made by SERAP Senior Programmes Officer, Folashade Arigbadu, during a capacity-building workshop on safety and security rights, accountability and access to justice organised by the organisation in Makurdi at the weekend. Arigbadu said the training, organised under SERAP’s People-Centered Public Safety project, was designed to strengthen community members’ capacity to identify security threats, engage security agencies and use lawful channels to demand accountability. She said the initiative was not intended to teach communities how to protect themselves, noting that residents already possessed valuable knowledge and strategies for responding to security challenges. “We know that community members already have some form of capacity. We are just here to enhance that capacity and ensure that what they are doing is lawful and can produce results,” she said. According to her, SERAP was particularly interested in understanding how communities in Guma and Katsina-Ala Local Government Areas had been responding to security challenges and how their existing efforts could be strengthened. “We need to do this with the people, not for the people. The people understand their communities better, so we want to work with them to strengthen what they already have,” she said. Arigbadu said Benue and Bayelsa states were selected for the first phase of the project following research into safety and security concerns in the two states. She added that the initiative would later be extended to other states and local government areas, noting that SERAP was already working towards establishing a similar structure in Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State. The SERAP official said participants included members of Community Policing Committees, with representatives of religious groups, women, youths, traditional institutions, community leaders and security agencies. She said the committees, provided for under the Police Act, offered communities a channel for communicating emerging security concerns to law enforcement agencies. “If there is something happening in the community, they have direct access to security agencies. They can report early warning signs and discuss how to prevent a situation from escalating,” she said. Arigbadu also urged citizens to pay closer attention to government expenditure on security, saying residents had the right to seek explanations when insecurity persisted despite public spending. “If the state government is getting money every year for security and people are still feeling insecure, they have a right to ask questions. What are you using the money to do? How are you deploying it?” she asked. She said citizens should also understand that responsibility for security did not rest solely with the Federal Government, adding that state governments had important roles to play. “They need to understand where responsibility lies and ask the right questions,” she said. Arigbadu explained that the training was also aimed at helping residents understand their rights, identify the appropriate authorities and use lawful channels to seek redress and accountability. During the workshop, the Lead, Legal, Lawyers Alert, Solumtochukwu Ozobulu, spoke to participants on community safety and security rights, while Assistant Team Lead, Legal, SERAP, Oluwakemi Agunbiade, trained them on the use of the Freedom of Information, FOI, Act, to obtain information from public institutions. Participants, including law students, traditional and religious leaders, commended SERAP for the initiative, saying the training had enhanced their understanding of their rights and responsibilities. A law student, David Mzer, said the workshop had equipped participants with knowledge to ask relevant questions and demand information from government. He added that participants had also learnt that some benefits they previously regarded as privileges were rights guaranteed by law, pledging to share the knowledge with other members of their communities. The post SERAP trains Benue communities on security tracking, accountability appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Clause 81 of Cocoa Board Bill infringes on farmers’ property rights – NPP
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has raised concerns about restrictions on the use of cocoa farmland under the newly passed Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, arguing that the provisions infringe on the property rights of farmers and landowners. Chairman of the NPP Policy Committee on Agriculture, Dr Isaac Yaw Opoku, says Clause 81 of the Bill places excessive restrictions on the ability of landowners to determine how their property should be used. Speaking at a press conference on Sunday, August 9, Dr Opoku argued that the provision could expose cocoa farmers to harassment, arbitrary arrests and extortion if allowed to become law in its current form. Clause 81 seeks to restrict the conversion or destruction of cocoa farms for purposes other than cocoa cultivation without prior authorisation. The provision effectively gives cocoa farms protected status and restricts landowners from converting cocoa plantations to alternative uses without the required approval, including where the farms are situated on private, family or stool lands. Dr Opoku questioned the justification for imposing such restrictions on farmers and landowners who have invested their own resources in acquiring and developing their properties. “It is our considered analysis that this provision is unenforceable as drafted and will lend itself to abuse, to arbitrary arrest, to extortion at the farm gate and to the harassment of an already struggling farming population,” he said. He argued that there was already evidence of the abuse of some provisions of Ghana’s criminal laws and expressed concern that cocoa farmers could face similar treatment if Clause 81 is implemented. “We say this against a background in which we are already witnessing the abuse of Sections 207 and 208 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960, Act 29,” he claimed. “We have no confidence that cocoa farmers will be spared,” he added. The NPP agriculture policy chairman further argued that preventing landowners from freely determining the use of their land without compensation raises fundamental property rights concerns. “These are significant infringements on private property rights imposed without compensation,” he stated. The NPP maintains that while measures may be necessary to protect Ghana’s cocoa industry and prevent the indiscriminate destruction of cocoa farms, such interventions should not disproportionately restrict the rights of farmers and landowners. The party has consequently called for further scrutiny and broader stakeholder consultation on the legislation before it receives presidential assent. Parliament passed the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, on Thursday, July 30, as part of reforms aimed at strengthening the governance and sustainability of the cocoa sector. The Bill is awaiting presidential assent.

items.title: Guiriko : La CNAVC sensibilise les habitants contre le paludisme
items.description: Guiriko : La CNAVC sensibilise les habitants contre le paludisme Bobo-Dioulasso, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Les membres de la Coordination nationale des associations de veille citoyenne (CNAVC)z, section Houet, en collaboration avec le chargé de mission à la présidence du Faso pour la région du Guiriko, Omar Traoré, ont mené, samedi, au secteur 15 de Bobo-Dioulasso, une campagne de sensibilisation et d’assainissement contre le paludisme et la dengue. L’activité a consisté notamment à sensibiliser les habitants sur l’importance de l’assainissement des concessions et à collecter les récipients usagés susceptibles de constituer des gîtes larvaires pour les moustiques. Le président de la CNAVC, section Houet, Ousmane Kindo, s’est réjoui de la mobilisation des bénévoles engagés dans l’opération. « Je suis très satisfait du travail accompli. Les membres de la CNAVC ont démontré leur profond patriotisme et leur engagement envers le Burkina Faso. Dès qu’ils ont été informés que les nids d’ordures étaient vecteurs de maladies, ils se sont immédiatement mobilisés sur le terrain », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, les volontaires se sont rendus dans les concessions pour sensibiliser les habitants et les inviter à adopter de bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et d’assainissement. Le directeur régional de la Santé, Issa Konaté, a souligné l’importance de la collecte des récipients usagés dans la prévention des maladies vectorielles. « J’ai vu les acteurs sur le terrain, en train de sensibiliser et de recueillir ces objets non utilisés qui sont des gîtes larvaires au niveau des ménages. Ces objets sont chargés dans les tricycles pour être transportés vers les lieux de destruction », a-t-il expliqué. Pour le directeur régional, cette opération contribue à réduire les lieux de reproduction des moustiques, vecteurs du paludisme et de la dengue. Il a appelé à la pérennisation de l’initiative et à une implication accrue des populations. « Cet appel a été fait par le gouvernement du Burkina. Je voudrais que cette activité puisse se perpétuer et que la communauté puisse comprendre que c’est à travers ces gestes simples que nous allons faire un grand bond dans la lutte contre le paludisme, parce que nous devons l’éliminer d’ici 2030. Chacun a un rôle à jouer et tout le monde doit rester engagé », a-t-il insisté. Bonaventure Ouédraogo, résident du secteur 15, a témoigné de la prise de conscience suscitée par l’opération au sein de son foyer. « On avait beaucoup de récipients ouverts, de vieilles marmites et de bidons inutilisables dans la cour, sans savoir qu’ils pouvaient constituer des gîtes larvaires. Nous sommes très contents de cette sensibilisation », a-t-il témoigné. Cette opération de sensibilisation et d’assainissement vise ainsi à renforcer la mobilisation communautaire contre les maladies vectorielles, particulièrement en cette période hivernale favorable à la prolifération des moustiques. Agence d'Information du Burkina CS/AB/wis

items.title: Curfew imposed in Balochistan Surab's district over law and order concerns
items.description: QUETTA: The district administration of Surab on Sunday imposed a curfew across the district till August 15, citing concerns over the law and order situation. According to an official notification, “The curfew will remain in force daily from 8pm to 9am during the specified period, starting from August 9 to 15, 2026.” The administration also directed citizens to avoid leaving their homes unnecessarily during curfew hours, fully cooperate with law enforcement agencies, and strictly follow the security standard operating procedures (SOPs) issued for the protection of their families. The notification warned that individuals violating the curfew would be responsible for any harm or loss resulting from their actions. Legal action would be taken against those found violating the restrictions, it added. Revised timings for Khuzdar commercial centres Meanwhile, the district administration of Khuzdar announced revised operating hours for commercial centres across the district amid growing security concerns. According to a notification issued by the office of the Khuzdar deputy commissioner, the measure had been taken temporarily as a precaution to protect the lives and property of citizens and the business community. Under the new order, all markets, shops, hotels and other commercial establishments in Khuzdar district will remain closed from 8pm to 10am daily. The order will be effective immediately and will remain in force until further directives. However, pharmacies, medical stores, private hospitals and other healthcare facilities have been exempted from the restriction because of the essential nature of their services. The district administration directed assistant commissioners, magistrates and police officials to ensure strict implementation of the order in their respective areas. The administration also urged traders and the public to cooperate with the authorities to help minimise potential security threats and ensure the safety of citizens and their property. Officials said the restrictions would be reviewed and amended only after an assessment of the security situation. Earlier this week, the district authorities in Kalat and Khuzdar directed traders and the business community to close shops in the evening and advised residents to remain indoors at night due to security concerns.

items.title: NPP urges Mahama not to assent to Cocoa Board Bill over ‘rushed’ passage
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called on President John Mahama not to assent to the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, but to return it to Parliament for broader stakeholder consultation. The party argues that the Bill was rushed through Parliament without sufficient engagement with cocoa farmers and other key stakeholders, despite provisions it says could have far-reaching implications for the cocoa industry. Ranking Member on Parliament’s Agriculture Committee and Co-Chairman of the NPP Policy Committee on Agriculture, Dr Isaac Yaw Opoku, made the call at a press conference at the party’s headquarters on Sunday, August 9, 2026. According to him, the Bill, which repeals the Ghana Cocoa Board Law, 1984 (PNDC Law 81), introduces significant changes, including new governance arrangements, the establishment of a tribunal and the creation of new offences. Dr Opoku said the Bill was laid before Parliament on July 28 and passed within the same week, arguing that the process did not provide enough time for meaningful consultation with cocoa farmers, landowners and other industry stakeholders. “We urge His Excellency the President to withhold his assent to the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, and return the same to Parliament for broader stakeholder consultation,” he said. NPP raises concern over cocoa tree restrictions The NPP also raised concerns about provisions restricting the destruction or uprooting of cocoa trees without prior authorisation. Dr Opoku argued that such a requirement could unnecessarily restrict farmers in managing their own farms and potentially expose them to sanctions for activities such as removing diseased, unproductive or moribund cocoa trees. He questioned why cocoa farmers should require prior approval from the Ghana Cocoa Board before removing trees they consider no longer productive or suitable for cultivation. According to him, any legislation that significantly affects the rights and operations of cocoa farmers should be subjected to extensive consultation before becoming law. The NPP warned that the consequences of the legislation could extend beyond current cocoa farmers and affect the future of an industry that remains important to Ghana’s economy. The party is therefore asking President Mahama to return the Bill to Parliament to allow for further scrutiny and broader engagement with farmers and other stakeholders before it is reconsidered.

items.title: Voyage en Algérie : 15 conseils du guide Lonely Planet aux touristes étrangers
items.description: Le célèbre guide de voyage australien Lonely Planet donne 15 conseils aux touristes qui souhaitent se rendre en Algérie. Visa, argent, sécurité, santé, tenue vestimentaire ou encore règles de bonne conduite, le site spécialisé dans le voyage revient sur plusieurs points à connaître avant de partir. Le guide présente l’Algérie comme un pays qui dispose d’une « côte méditerranéenne longue de 1 200 km » et de « montagnes enneigées du haut plateau de l’Atlas saharien ». Il met en avant la diversité des paysages, entre le littoral, les montagnes et le Sahara. Mais avant de s’y rendre, Lonely Planet recommande de bien préparer son séjour, notamment concernant les documents de voyage, la santé et les règles à respecter. Visiter l’Algérie : ce qu’il faut savoir selon Lonely Planet En premier lieu, le guide rappelle que le visa est nécessaire pour « la plupart des voyageurs étrangers ». Pour effectuer les démarches, Lonely Planet recommande de consulter le site de la mission diplomatique ou consulaire algérienne dans le pays de résidence. Une exception concerne les voyages organisés dans le Sahara. Un « visa de régularisation » peut être délivré à l’arrivée, avec un tarif à partir de 110 euros. En amont, les touristes doivent se rapprocher d’une agence de voyage afin d’obtenir une « autorisation d’embarquement », précise le guide. Concernant la période du voyage, tout dépend de l’activité prévue et de la région visitée. Pour découvrir le Sahara, Lonely Planet recommande la période entre octobre et avril. Pour profiter du littoral, la période estivale, de juin à septembre, est privilégiée. Les mois de juin et septembre sont également recommandés pour éviter l’affluence des touristes locaux et des Algériens établis à l’étranger qui rentrent au pays en juillet et août, ainsi que la hausse des prix des prestations et des produits durant cette période. Pour les amateurs de randonnée et de nature, le printemps et l’automne sont davantage conseillés, notamment pour découvrir le Djurdjura et les monts de l’Aurès. Le guide conseille aussi d’éviter, si possible, la période du ramadan, durant laquelle certains restaurants ferment en journée et l’activité tourne au ralenti. Les soirées restent toutefois animées. En Algérie, l’argent liquide reste privilégié S’agissant des dépenses, l’argent liquide reste le principal moyen de paiement en Algérie. Les cartes bancaires étrangères sont peu acceptées. Certains hôtels et restaurants internationaux font toutefois exception. Lonely Planet recommande donc aux touristes de prévoir suffisamment d’espèces pour leur séjour. Le guide rappelle également que les voyageurs étrangers doivent déclarer à leur arrivée les sommes supérieures à 5 000 euros. Les dinars algériens ne peuvent, eux, pas être sortis du pays. Pour le change, Lonely Planet indique que les opérations officielles se font auprès des banques. Une vigilance recommandée Concernant la sécurité, Lonely Planet décrit l’Algérie comme un pays « globalement sûr », tout en appelant les touristes à respecter certaines précautions. Le guide recommande notamment de consulter les conseils aux voyageurs du ministère des Affaires étrangères. Il mentionne aussi les risques de vols à l’arraché et de pickpockets dans les endroits fréquentés. Les femmes qui voyagent seules peuvent, elles, attirer davantage l’attention. Lonely Planet leur conseille notamment d’éviter de marcher seules la nuit et de fréquenter les rues désertes ou peu éclairées Pour la santé, les établissements de santé sont jugés globalement corrects, avec des différences entre les structures publiques et privées. Lonely Planet souligne également que les pharmacies sont nombreuses et généralement bien approvisionnées. Le guide recommande aux touristes de prévoir de l’argent liquide en cas de besoin médical et de souscrire une assurance santé pour leur séjour. Des règles à respecter L’Algérie est décrite comme un pays « globalement conservateur ». Concernant la tenue vestimentaire, Lonely Planet recommande notamment aux voyageuses de couvrir leurs épaules et de privilégier les pantalons ou les jupes longues, en particulier dans certains lieux religieux. Les habitudes peuvent également varier sur les plages, surtout dans celles fréquentées principalement par les familles. Les démonstrations d’affection sont peu appréciées en public, particulièrement pour les couples non mariés. La consommation d’alcool sur la voie publique est interdite. Certains hôtels et restaurants en proposent toutefois. Marchandage et pourboire Dans les marchés, le marchandage est possible, par exemple pour les vêtements, les souvenirs et certains produits artisanaux. Lonely Planet recommande toutefois de rester courtois lors des négociations et de refuser poliment lorsque le prix ne convient pas. Le pourboire n’est, lui, pas une pratique systématique en Algérie. Attention aux photos Le guide rappelle que certains bâtiments ne peuvent pas être photographiés, notamment les commissariats, les gendarmeries et les installations liées à l’armée. Il déconseille également de prendre en photo ou de filmer des agents en uniforme ou leurs véhicules. Découvrir le patrimoine algérien Lonely Planet conseille aux touristes de consacrer du temps aux musées, aux sites historiques et aux différents vestiges présents dans le pays. Le guide met en avant les différentes facettes de l’Algérie, entre mer, montagnes et désert, ainsi que les traces laissées par les différentes civilisations qui ont marqué son histoire. Durant leur séjour, les touristes sont invités à faire preuve de patience et de souplesse face aux imprévus. Les changements de programme ou certaines démarches peuvent être difficiles à anticiper. Lonely Planet recommande donc de rester calme et de privilégier une attitude respectueuse avec le personnel et les agents des services publics. L’accueil et la générosité des Algériens mis en avant Enfin, Lonely Planet met en avant l’accueil et la générosité des Algériens. Le guide décrit des habitants disponibles et prêts à aider les touristes qui souhaitent découvrir le pays et sa culture. Il estime également qu’un effort pour respecter les habitudes locales permet de faciliter les échanges durant le séjour. L’article Voyage en Algérie : 15 conseils du guide Lonely Planet aux touristes étrangers est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Amin Adam congratulates Agalga, pledges constructive Minority engagement
items.description: Former Finance Minister and Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has congratulated James Agalga on his selection as the new Majority Leader, expressing confidence in his ability to lead the Majority caucus effectively. Dr Amin Adam said Mr Agalga’s years of experience in Parliament and government had equipped him with a firm understanding of the demands of parliamentary leadership. In a Facebook post on Sunday, August 9, he described the Builsa North MP as a fine intellectual and formidable debater whose qualities would benefit the work of Parliament. “I have known James since his younger days, and I can say without hesitation that he comes to this role well prepared. His years in Parliament and in Government have given him a firm grasp of the demands of leadership,” he wrote. “He is also a fine intellect and a formidable debater, which are the qualities the House will benefit from.” Dr Amin Adam also reaffirmed the Minority’s commitment to fulfilling its constitutional responsibilities, including holding the government accountable, defending democratic principles and representing the interests of Ghanaians. He, however, expressed hope that the new Majority leadership would work constructively with the Minority and prioritise dialogue and consensus-building on issues of national importance. “Ultimately, I believe the leaders on both sides will engage in greater dialogue and build consensus where it matters, so that our discourse serves the higher interest of our country,” he said. Mr Agalga’s selection as Majority Leader follows changes to the leadership of the Majority caucus in Parliament.

items.title: Kénédougou : Les populations de Morolaba renforcent la prévention contre le paludisme
items.description: Kénédougou : Les populations de Morolaba renforcent la prévention contre le paludisme Morolaba, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Les populations de la commune de Morolaba ont participé, ce samedi, à une vaste opération d’assainissement et de sensibilisation au centre de santé et de promotion sociale dans le cadre de la Journée nationale de lutte anti-vectorielle, en vue de contribuer à la prévention du paludisme. La journée a été marquée par des séances de sensibilisation sur les mesures de prévention du paludisme, le nettoyage de l’environnement et la destruction des gîtes larvaires favorisant la prolifération des moustiques. Les participants ont procédé au curage de certains points de stagnation d’eau et au nettoyage des alentours du CSPS tout en invitant les populations à maintenir leur cadre de vie propre afin de réduire les risques de propagation du paludisme. Selon les organisateurs, la lutte contre les moustiques passe par l’adoption de gestes simples d’assainissement et l’élimination régulière des gîtes larvaires. Le PDS Germain Mien a indiqué que cette mobilisation traduit l’engagement des autorités communales, des services de santé et des populations de Morolaba à soutenir les actions de prévention du paludisme et de promotion de la santé communautaire. items.title: Anger mounts in US over vast network of car license plate cameras
items.description: In only a few years, the surveillance start-up Flock has installed more than 100,000 license plate reader cameras across the United States. But a grassroots movement upset over privacy concerns is fighting back — even going so far as systematically vandalising the equipment. The first time he decided to trash one of the cameras, a self-styled vigilante wearing all black and known as Nomark says he was “super nervous”. Now, after disabling about 30 of the devices near his home in the Minneapolis area, he told AFP : “I’m not really as scared anymore.” Flock cameras are installed by police departments, homeowners’ associations and businesses, ostensibly to catch criminals in the act. Data is uploaded to Flock’s cloud and can be shared with subscribers. But opponents are outraged at what they say is a dangerous tool that can be used to infringe on American privacy and civil liberties. At just 20 years old, Nomark offers his 500,000 Instagram followers a how-to guide for rendering the cameras useless, raising awareness about the devices. His detractors point out — correctly — that his actions are illegal, but like-minded individuals have followed suit nationwide over the past few weeks. Instead of being dismissed as a radical fringe outfit, the anti-Flock movement is taking hold. Its proponents have been active online for months, creating crowdsourced maps of cameras, sharing ways to block their lenses, and hailing the “heroes” who are arrested for destroying them. The Facebook group DeFlock America has more than 600,000 members, and is gaining thousands more by the day. Massive database Flock cameras differ from traditional surveillance cameras in that they do not record video footage. Instead, they take still images of vehicles, capturing the make, model, colour, license plate data and other distinguishing features such as bumper stickers. And unlike classic surveillance cameras, which are not networked, this data is stored for up to a month and shareable, sometimes across state lines. Opponents say this gives police an overwhelming look into the private lives of law-abiding Americans. Jon Bridges, a police official in Virginia’s state capital Richmond, says that for “practically any crime that has a connection with a vehicle or a vehicle involved, we will at least query the database to see if there’s anything there”. His department has used Flock since 2023. Bridges gave an example of how useful the technology can be: during the investigation of a domestic-related double homicide in May, police quickly identified a suspect who fled the scene in his pick-up truck. Detectives retrieved his license plate data and entered an alert in Flock’s system. When he appeared on another camera, officers in a neighbouring county arrested him. Potential abuses Detractors fear that this allows officers to track vehicles without warrants, opening the door to a host of possible abuses of power. According to an investigation done by The Washington Post , at least 50 police officers have been accused of misusing the Flock system, most of them to spy on the comings and goings of their romantic partners or exes. In other cases reported in US media, cops used Flock to track women who had abortions — illegal in several US states. Some illegally sent data from the system to immigration agents. Flock CEO Garrett Langley has accused some opponents of being “terrorists,” stoking the fire. “There is really an incredible grassroots movement against Flock,” said Chad Marlow, senior policy counsel for the American Civil Liberties Union, calling its growth “stunning”. The movement has support on both the political left and right, notably from libertarians. Former Fox News host and conservative heavyweight Tucker Carlson has called the vandals “decent, patriotic Americans” who are simply “taking matters into their own hands.” Across the country, local groups are pushing their lawmakers to step back from Flock. Steven Keener, a professor of criminology at Christopher Newport University in Virginia, said residents can meet with city council members or mayors to convince them to cancel their contracts with the surveillance company. So far, such grassroots efforts are proving successful. From Los Angeles to small towns in Virginia, more than 70 municipalities have ended their association with Flock in recent months, according to an ACLU tally. For Keener, the movement stands out in a country riven by political divisions. “Because decisions are at the local level, people realise that they can actually make a difference,” he told AFP .

items.title: Ondo Central: Return Akinyelure to senate, Adebumiti urges voters
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — Political analyst and grassroots advocate, Adedotun Adebumiti, has urged voters in Ondo Central Senatorial District to support the African Democratic Congress, ADC, candidate and former Senator Ayo Akinyelure in the 2027 election. Adebumiti, who spoke with journalists in Ifedore Local Government Area of Ondo State, said Akinyelure’s previous tenure in the Senate was characterised by what he described as employment opportunities, community development and accessibility to constituents. He said the call for Akinyelure’s return was based on his record of service rather than political party affiliation. “Akinyelure’s open-door policy allowed constituents to easily communicate their needs and concerns. That is essential for effective representation,” Adebumiti said. He described the former senator’s tenure between 2011 and 2015 as beneficial to communities across the six local government areas that make up the senatorial district. Adebumiti urged voters to consider candidates’ records and accessibility when making their choice in the 2027 election. “He has the credibility and the passion. When he was in office, he employed many people, from civil defence to immigration and the police. You cannot go to any local government in Ondo Central without meeting someone who benefited from employment opportunities,” he said. Adebumiti also criticised what he described as shortcomings in the distribution of empowerment opportunities under the current representation, alleging that some names were removed from beneficiaries’ lists. He said elected representatives should ensure that their programmes and interventions were accessible to all constituents, regardless of political affiliation. Adebumiti further argued that Akinyelure’s history of contesting and winning elections on different political platforms demonstrated what he described as his personal appeal and commitment to public service. items.title: Danyi : Le chef du canton d’Ahlon reçoit son décret de reconnaissance
items.description: Apéyémé, 9 août (ATOP) – Le chef du canton d’Ahlon dans la commune Danyi 2, Togbui Yao Lébénê Golo Gassou V a reçu son décret de reconnaissance le confirmant dans ses fonctions le vendredi 8 août. La cérémonie de remise a été présidée par le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Gal Dadja Maganawé, en présence du préfet de Danyi Koumagnanou Amavi, des députés, sénateurs, et autres autorités administratives, militaires, traditionnelles, religieuses. Vue partielle des chefs traditionnels En lui remettant le décret, le Général Maganawé a réaffirmé l’engagement constant du gouvernement sous le leadership du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé à la promotion et au rayonnement de la chefferie traditionnelle. Il a fait savoir qu’un chef traditionnel est un maillon essentiel et primordial de la conservation du patrimoine culturel et du maintien de la cohésion sociale dans sa communauté. Le gouverneur a rappelé au nouveau chef son rôle en tant que gardien des us et coutumes et son devoir face à l’administration centrale. Il a insisté sur l’obligation de réserve, d’impartialité et de neutralité à laquelle, il doit se soumettre vis à vis de ses administrés. Le gouverneur a exhorté la population à travailler en harmonie avec le nouveau chef en vue de l’exécution de sa mission. Le doyen des chefs traditionnels du canton, Togbui Agnégué Kodjo Apim IX a félicité le nouveau chef et lui a renouvelé la confiance et le soutien de la population dans l’accomplissement de sa mission. Togbui Gassou V a remercié le Président du Conseil pour l’importance qu’il attache à la sauvegarde des us et coutumes. Il a promis d’assurer sa fonction avec fidélité, loyauté et justice en vue d’un développement harmonieux du canton. ATOP/SKD/BA/BV

items.title: Sebta : les autorités continuent de recenser les mineurs, des centres dédiés pour protéger les filles
items.description: La situation des mineurs à Sebta occupée continue de se tendre après l’arrivée massive enregistrée la semaine dernière. Les autorités espagnoles ont recensé 1.342 mineurs dans la ville, un chiffre encore susceptible d’augmenter alors que les opérations d’identification et d’enregistrement se poursuivent. La police espagnole procède actuellement à l’identification des enfants pris en charge, tandis que certains mineurs se trouveraient encore dans les rues ou hébergés dans des logements privés. La grande majorité des nouveaux arrivants sont âgés de 16 à 17 ans, mais les autorités font également état de la présence d’enfants de moins de 12 ans. L’ampleur du phénomène apparaît d’autant plus importante qu’au début du mois de juillet, les structures d’accueil de Sebta ne comptaient qu’environ 180 mineurs. En l’espace d’un mois, leur nombre a donc été multiplié par plus de sept, mettant les capacités d’hébergement de la ville sous forte pression. Des structures séparées pour les filles Face à l’arrivée d’un nombre important de jeunes filles, les autorités locales ont dû aménager des espaces spécifiques afin de les protéger et de les séparer des autres groupes de mineurs. Deux établissements scolaires sont notamment utilisés pour leur hébergement et leur prise en charge. Cette mesure intervient alors que les autorités locales font état de préoccupations liées aux risques d’agressions sexuelles et d’exploitation. Selon des médias locaux, dont « El Faro de Ceuta » , la police enquête notamment sur un cas présumé de viol, tandis que les autorités n’excluent pas l’existence d’autres situations nécessitant des investigations. La priorité affichée est désormais de protéger les mineurs considérés comme les plus vulnérables, notamment les plus jeunes et les filles, dans un contexte où les structures d’accueil sont largement dépassées. Une capacité d’accueil sous forte pression Le gouvernement de Sebta souhaite accélérer le transfert d’une partie des mineurs vers la péninsule espagnole afin de réduire la pression exercée sur les infrastructures locales. Selon les autorités, le niveau de saturation actuel dépasse très largement les capacités habituelles de la ville. La ministre espagnole de la Jeunesse et de l’Enfance, Sira Rego, s’est rendue vendredi à Sebta et a reconnu la difficulté de la situation, tout en affirmant que celle-ci commençait à se stabiliser. La responsable gouvernementale a également salué la mobilisation des habitants de la ville, dont plusieurs ont accueilli des enfants arrivés lors de la crise, et exprimé sa tristesse face aux pertes humaines enregistrées durant les tentatives d’accès à Sebta. Madrid n’exclut pas une coopération avec le Maroc Sira Rego a assuré que le gouvernement espagnol entendait garantir la prise en charge de l’ensemble des mineurs présents à Sebta, en donnant la priorité aux enfants les plus vulnérables. Interrogée sur une éventuelle coopération avec le Maroc concernant la situation de ces mineurs, la ministre a indiqué que Madrid était disposé à examiner tout mécanisme de coopération, à condition que les droits des enfants et leur intérêt supérieur soient respectés. Elle a également affirmé que l’Espagne ne s’opposait pas, par principe, à un éventuel retour de certains mineurs au Maroc, précisant que les autorités espagnoles se concentraient avant tout sur la protection de leurs droits. Cette question intervient alors que Sebta fait face à une situation exceptionnelle après l’arrivée de milliers de personnes lors de la récente crise migratoire, avec des conséquences particulièrement lourdes sur les capacités d’accueil et de protection des mineurs. items.title: HRF Report: Nigeria now full authoritarian state — APM
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has cited a report by the Human Rights Foundation (HRF) to declare that Nigeria is now a ‘full authoritarian state’, calling for international sanctions against officials allegedly undermining democracy and urging Nigerians to vote out the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027. The party said the warning was no longer about ordinary political disagreements, alleging that democratic institutions, security and anti-corruption agencies and the courts were being deployed against opposition parties and dissenting voices, while citizens were increasingly losing confidence in the country’s democratic system. APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, made the position known in a statement on Sunday, saying the party’s earlier warnings about what it described as authoritarian tendencies had been reinforced by the HRF’s Tyranny Tracker report. “The report confirms APM’s position that under President Tinubu, Nigeria’s constitutional democracy and democratic institutions have been captured by executive authoritarianism,” Yusuf said. The party called on the United Nations, European Union, African Union, Commonwealth, United States, United Kingdom, France and other international partners to intervene diplomatically, including through visa bans, asset freezes and other measures against Nigerian officials it accused of undermining democracy. APM also alleged that security agencies had been used to suppress protests and criticism, with citizens allegedly killed, beaten, arrested, detained or charged with treason. It further claimed that more than 628,000 Nigerians had been killed and 2.2 million abducted during the period under review, amid continued attacks by terrorists on communities. On press freedom, the party alleged that about 100 journalists had been brutalised or detained while covering pro-democracy protests or engaging in critical reporting. “Today in Nigeria, freedom of expression and the media have been suppressed with about 100 journalists brutalized and detained by authorities for covering pro-democracy protests or critical reporting,” it said. The APM also accused the government of restricting opposition parties by allegedly using security agencies to intimidate, harass, detain and prosecute opposition leaders, while denying them access to venues for political mobilisation. It alleged that in some APC-controlled states, opposition parties were also being denied access to media platforms and prevented from erecting campaign billboards. The party’s concerns extended to the electoral process, with APM questioning the credibility of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. It accused INEC, under its chairman, Prof. Josiah Amupitan, of undue interference in the internal affairs of opposition parties and alleged refusal to obey court orders favourable to them. “Currently, majority of Nigerians have lost hope in the integrity of INEC as presently constituted, to conduct credible general elections that will reflect the Will of the people in 2027,” the party said. APM also accused the APC-led National Assembly of failing to adequately check executive power, describing it as a “rubber stamp” for the administration. On the economy, the party said Nigerians and businesses were facing mounting pressure from multiple taxes, indirect levies and revenue-collection practices it described as harassment. It warned that the combination of insecurity, economic hardship and what it described as shrinking democratic space could produce a wider crisis, with consequences for Nigeria and neighbouring countries. “The APM is worried that the current situation in Nigeria, if not addressed, might lead to a crisis of monumental proposition capable of derailing our nation’s democracy and triggering a large-scale humanitarian disaster,” Yusuf said. The party urged Nigerians, civil society organisations, opposition parties, the media and other organised groups to unite against what it described as authoritarianism, while insisting that resistance must remain within the law. It urged Nigerians to make the 2027 general elections a decisive opportunity to change the government and elect what it described as a truly democratic and people-oriented administration on the APM platform. “Nigerians must use the 2027 general elections as a decisive opportunity to vote in a truly democratic and people-oriented government on the platform of the APM,” the party said. items.title: Accord rejects Tinubu endorsement claim
items.description: The Lagos State Chairman of Accord, Mr Dele Oladeji, has dismissed claims that the party endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid for 2027. Oladeji, also Secretary of the Forum of Accord Party Chairmen in Southern Nigeria, described the claim as false and contrary to the party’s position. He spoke on Sunday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) while reacting to remarks by Prof. Christopher Imumolen. Imumolen, a factional Accord presidential candidate, had reportedly claimed that the party was backing Tinubu for a second term in office. Oladeji said no National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting of the party had discussed or approved any endorsement of Tinubu. “Accord did not and will not endorse Tinubu for a second term. Any person claiming otherwise is playing politics or engaging in anti-party activities,” he said. According to him, the party has never deliberated on supporting Tinubu at any NEC meeting since preparations for 2027 began. “Accord has not at any time discussed any endorsement of President Tinubu at any of our NEC meetings. “So, there is no basis whatsoever for anybody to claim that Accord has endorsed President Tinubu,” he said. The chairman described Imumolen’s position as a personal opinion aimed at attracting public attention rather than reflecting the party’s official stance. “Chris Imumolen is impersonating the Accord presidential candidate and declaring support for President Tinubu is political shadow boxing for media attention,” he said. Oladeji also questioned Imumolen’s membership status, alleging that his name was absent from the party’s current membership register. He claimed that an older register had been replaced by a new membership register introduced in 2023 by the national leadership. “His name is not on the Accord membership register, as the register he was on had been phased out,” Oladeji said. He challenged Imumolen to provide evidence of his membership and participation in recognised party structures and activities. “If Imumolen claims otherwise, let him publish his Accord membership register and pictures of any NEC meeting attended by INEC officials,” he said. Oladeji stressed that Accord remained committed to contesting the 2027 general elections across all levels of government. He said the party would field candidates for state assembly, governorship, House of Representatives, Senate and presidential elections nationwide. “Accord candidates will contest every elective position in the country, including the presidential election,” he said. The chairman argued that endorsing another party’s presidential candidate would contradict Accord’s political objectives and identity. “Only an unserious person and political party will endorse the candidate of another party. Accord will not do such,” he said. Oladeji urged members and supporters to disregard reports suggesting the party had entered any agreement supporting Tinubu’s re-election campaign. He maintained that Accord’s official position could only emerge through decisions reached by its constitutional organs and recognised meetings. According to him, individuals making contrary claims should be regarded as acting outside the established position of the party. Oladeji reiterated that Accord would remain independent and pursue its programmes and electoral ambitions ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post Accord rejects Tinubu endorsement claim appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kénédougou : Les VDP agricoles de Djigouèra espèrent une récolte satisfaisante sur leur champ de cinq hectares
items.description: Kénédougou : Les VDP agricoles de Djigouèra espèrent une récolte satisfaisante sur leur champ de cinq hectares Djigouèra, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Les Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP) agricoles de la commune de Djigouèra affichent leur optimisme quant à l’issue de la campagne agricole 2026. Sur leur champ collectif de cinq hectares aménagés à Soubagagnedougou, l’évolution de plusieurs spéculations laisse entrevoir des perspectives encourageantes. Selon le responsable des VDP agricoles de Djigouèra, Sékou Amed Traoré, le site est exploité avec cinq spéculations réparties sur l’ensemble de la superficie. Le riz occupe 1,5 hectares, tandis que le maïs, le niébé et le soja couvrent chacun un hectare. L’arachide est cultivée sur une superficie de 0,5 hectare. « Nous sommes confiants pour cette campagne au regard de l’évolution de certaines spéculations », a déclaré le camarade Traoré. Il a toutefois relevé que les cultures de niébé et de soja connaissent un développement moins satisfaisant. En revanche, les parcelles de riz, de maïs et d’arachide présentent un état végétatif jugé encourageant, suscitant l’espoir d’une bonne production à la fin de la campagne. Malgré ces contraintes, les VDP poursuivent les travaux d’entretien du champ et restent mobilisés pour optimiser les rendements. Agence d'information du Burkina AKK/AK/wis

items.title: Solenzo : destruction des gîtes larvaires, le Haut-Commissaire donne le top départ
items.description: Solenzo : destruction des gîtes larvaires, le Haut-Commissaire donne le top départ Solenzo, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Haut-Commissaire de la province des Banwa Sanfiénalé Joseph Sirima a donné ce samedi 8 août 2026, le top départ des Journées nationales de destruction des gîtes larvaires en procédant symboliquement au bouchage des flaques d'eau stagnante devant la préfecture de Solenzo. Cette activité de salubrité publique s'est déroulée en présence du personnel de la santé, des directeurs et chefs de service, des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie, des VDP agricoles et de la population de Solenzo. Dans une brève allocution le premier responsable de la province a rappelé l'importance de cette campagne dans la lutte contre le paludisme et les maladies liées à la prolifération des moustiques, principaux vecteurs de transmission. Le Haut-Commissaire Sirima a par la suite invité, l'ensemble de la population de Solenzo à s'approprier cette initiative nationale en procédant dans leurs concessions respectives ainsi que dans les artères de la ville, à la fermeture systématique des eaux stagnantes, foyers privilégiés de reproduction des moustiques. Il a exhorté les populations à un changement de comportement durable, gage d'un environnement sain et d'une meilleure protection contre les maladies liées à l'insalubrité. Agence d'Information du Burkina SO/wis
